parsed.why: Broad public-accommodation protections, gender-neutral bathrooms, and shield laws materially improve local conditions. National passport, entry-screening, facility, and custody exposures still govern parts of the visit; the county sports restriction is a limited additional negative.

Statewide protections, no adult facility ban, and a court ruling supporting a student's facility access mitigate the national regime. National travel-facing restrictions remain; university compliance with sports restrictions and weaker local recourse leave this below the strongest protective divisions.

No statewide adult facility ban, but protections are absent in most localities, hate-crime coverage is missing, and document changes leave records. Appointed-board restrictions and limited recourse add local exposure to the severe national framework.

Enforced public-accommodation protections, gender-identity hate-crime coverage, and shield laws offer meaningful local safeguards. These do not displace national entry, document, facility, and custody risks; local enforcement evidence is limited.

The operative facility law excludes trans visitors from multi-occupancy spaces by birth sex, a direct, recurring state exposure; discrimination protections are scant and the state is rated among the worst for anti-trans legislation. National restrictions compound it.
